text:
Emil Heineman is the Islanders' hitter with a shooter's shot. He has 63 hits in 24 games, a top shot speed in the 92nd percentile per NHL EDGE, and a short-handed goal in Winnipeg on Nov. 19 that put New York ahead. What he doesn't have yet is the goals: three, after 22 last season.

His shooting is part of it (10% against 13% last season), but so is shot quality. His individual expected goals per 60 have fallen from 0.89 last season to 0.59, so the looks have thinned, not just the finishing. Oddly, his linemates have been finishing well above their chances with him on, which is propping up his six assists.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains what he was last season: 6.6 chances per 60 from the home-plate area in front of the net, 86th percentile. Evolving-Hockey also had him drawing more penalties than he takes. Watch whether he gets back to the net front; that's where his goals came from.
